text: THE READING ROOM公開コード・データ / Public code and data Site coverage and counting rules Published web edition, counted 2026-11-24. These are counts of catalog entries and documented examples, not a claim that every entry is a verified end-to-end solver. 72 equation/model entries · 144 methods and building blocks · 249 journal/conference papers · 310 total sources. There are 9 saved-profile equation-gallery cases across 7 equation families, and 141 reading chapters including this inventory. Equations and models# Named equation/model entries, not scalar component equations or mathematically disjoint families. Includes frameworks and auxiliary formulations; variants share one entry except the three separately explained SR/GR fluid systems. Biological entries are imported once from their own catalog. 50 entries have scoped local examples; 22 are reading-only, including all 22 biological survey entries. A coupled system is one entry; its individual component equations do not increase the count. Poisson/Laplace and dimensional variants share entries. Named frameworks and specialized kinetic laws can both appear, so this is not a count of mathematically disjoint families. Biological model survey# Logistic population growth — Reading only. The linked original is the later 1847 memoir; the 1838 note itself was not audited. The differential equation is not the discrete logistic map. Michaelis–Menten and full enzyme kinetics — Reading only. The 1913 rapid-equilibrium interpretation and the 1925 quasi-steady-state derivation must remain distinct. Lotka–Volterra predator–prey — Reading only. McKendrick age-structured population — Reading only. This is the classical age-transport form; the later von Foerster lineage is acknowledged without treating its date as the first appearance. SIR and SEIR compartment models — Reading only. The original general epidemic framework is broader than this SIR specialization. Population-count and fraction conventions give different β definitions. Fisher–KPP invasion front — Reading only. Fisher–KPP is a conventional family name; the independent KPP 1937 original remains an archival follow-up. The exact special speed is not the minimal speed. Monod growth and chemostat — Reading only. This writes one constant-yield extension of saturation growth, not a universal metabolic model. Hodgkin–Huxley membrane dynamics — Reading only. The original squid-axon model is not a calibrated human cardiac model. No single rate parameter set is selected by this survey. Turing reaction–diffusion framework — Reading only. A spot image or unequal diffusion coefficients alone do not establish a Turing mechanism. Boundary conditions determine the available modes. FitzHugh–Nagumo excitation and recovery — Reading only. This is a common normalized variant; cubic coefficients, recovery signs and nondimensionalization differ between formulations. Keller–Segel chemotaxis — Reading only. This is a common two-field reduction of a more detailed original formulation. Blowup thresholds depend on dimension, domain, boundary and chemical dynamics. Gierer–Meinhardt activator–inhibitor — Reading only. Source densities, saturation and baseline production vary across the model family. This simplified formula is not a verbatim transcription of every original variant. Fluid–elastic structure and immersed boundaries — Reading only. Immersed boundary is a numerical coupling method, not itself a closed biological constitutive equation. The existing periodic MAC solver does not implement this coupling. Chemical master equation and Gillespie SSA — Reading only. The 1977 paper is a foundational SSA reference, not a priority claim for all master equations. SSA is a solver; the reaction network is the model. A seed documents a trajectory, not an ensemble validation. Mackey–Glass delayed physiological feedback — Reading only. A scalar initial value alone is insufficient. The delayed ODE is distinct from a spatial reaction–diffusion model. Replicator evolutionary game dynamics — Reading only. No universal Lyapunov function or equivalence of fixed point and evolutionarily stable strategy is assumed. Schnakenberg reaction–diffusion — Reading only. A mathematical chemical pattern model; matching a visual biological pattern does not calibrate it to a tissue. Shigesada–Kawasaki–Teramoto cross-diffusion — Reading only. The displayed homogeneous-environment reduction omits the original environmental-potential terms. It is not equivalent to two independent scalar diffusion equations. Gray–Scott spatial autocatalysis — Reading only. 1983 is the well-mixed CSTR source; Pearson 1993 is the spatial pattern reference. Spot division does not by itself demonstrate cell division or a linear Turing instability. Aliev–Panfilov cardiac excitation — Reading only. Monodomain/bidomain tissue models add conductivity tensors and, for bidomain, an extracellular elliptic constraint. They are not automatically included by this two-variable model. Repressilator mRNA–protein network — Reading only. The six-variable form is distinct from a reduced three-protein oscillator; oscillations are parameter-dependent. Genetic toggle switch — Reading only. Bistability is not guaranteed for arbitrary Hill exponents or production rates. Induction, mRNA dynamics and noise are additional model choices. Numerical method inventory# Named numerical methods and building blocks with a reading chapter. Aliases count once; RK stages, dimensions, parameter combinations, mesh layouts and theoretical conditions do not add methods. A family and a separately explained algorithm may both appear. Not a count of mutually exclusive end-to-end solvers. 129 entries have scoped local examples; 15 are reading-only. Reconstruction limiters, preconditioners and coupling operators are building blocks, not complete PDE solvers. Mesh layouts, CFL conditions and theorems are not counted as numerical methods. Reproduction# The named registry is catalog/coverage.json; biological entries and publication types come from their respective catalogs. python scripts/build_coverage.py checks unique publication identities and local reading links, then generates the counts and this inventory. The website build runs that audit before rendering. Parameter choices, time frames, repeated equations in prose and test function counts do not increase these totals.
